item.research_question: How does the local destruction of short-range order (SRO) by dislocation glide lead to a rejuvenated state and influence the reversibility of planar defects (stacking faults and twin boundaries) in CrCoNi medium entropy alloys?
item.material_system: Equiatomic CrCoNi medium entropy alloy (MEA) and pure Ni single crystal
item.processing_route: Water-quenched from 1200 °C for 48 h; twin-jet electrochemical polishing; FIB lift-out to MEMS chips; FIB patterning to create sharp crack; in situ push-to-pull cyclic loading in TEM at room temperature (300 K)
item.test_conditions: Cyclic uniaxial tensile loading at room temperature (300 K); 1000 cycles; strain rate of 1 × 10^8 s^-1 in MD simulations; 300 keV electron beam for 4D-STEM; 15 eV and 20 eV energy filter slits
key_findings: Average stacking fault (SF) length increased from 17.5 nm to 48.3 nm in the first cycle (t=T/2) but retracted to 22 nm upon unloading (t=T), indicating reversibility.
After 1000 cycles, SFs became irreversible with average length reaching 67.1 nm and twin boundaries reaching 124.2 nm at zero external load.
SF energy in pure Ni is approximately 120 mJ/m², while in CrCoNi MEA it is approximately 13.3 mJ/m² initially.
MD simulations show SF reversibility changes occur after around 20 cycles when SF energy drops below a threshold value.
Ni-Cr and Co-Co atomic pairs are insensitive to mechanical loading, while other SRO types show a steady decrease with cycle number.
Residual hydrostatic tensile strain ahead of the crack tip increased in Ni but decreased in CrCoNi MEA due to SF-mediated plasticity.
CrCoNi MEA showed more significant crack-tip blunting after 1000 cycles compared to Ni, suggesting rejuvenation promotes ductility.
item.mechanism: Dislocation glide destroys local short-range order (SRO) on specific glide planes, leading to a rejuvenated state with higher entropy and free energy. This reduction in SRO lowers the stacking fault (SF) energy, making SFs and twin boundaries energetically favorable and irreversible, creating 'soft' zones that enhance damage tolerance.
item.limitations: The study primarily focuses on quasi 2-dimensional models due to the constraints of in-situ TEM thin samples; the role of excess vacancies in defect evolution is considered minimal and possibly negligible.
item.future_work: Further studies on pure metals with low SF energy (like Cu) for comparison; identifying strategies to optimize the degree and distribution of SRO in MEAs/HEAs to coordinate local rejuvenation processes.
quotes: Surprisingly, stacking faults (SFs) and twin boundaries (TBs) are reversible in initial cycles but become irreversible after a thousand cycles, indicating SF energy reduction and rejuvenation.
The reduction of the degree of SRO due to deformation leads to the continuous reduction of general SF energy near the crack tip.
The local rejuvenation in MEAs during deformation converts the material into a composite material with effectively 'soft' and 'hard' zones that increase the diversity of plasticity mechanisms.
